title: Discussion Tracker: Supporting Teacher Learning about Students’ Collaborative Argumentation in High School Classrooms
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of helping teachers support and assess collaborative argumentation in classroom discussion. The authors argue that teachers often struggle to track important features of student talk in real time and to reflect on discussion quality afterward, motivating a tool that automatically analyzes transcripts and presents usable feedback.

The intervention, Discussion Tracker (DT), is a classroom discussion analytics system that uses NLP models to classify student discourse along three dimensions: argument moves, specificity, and collaboration. DT generates visual summaries, coded transcripts, collaboration maps, strengths/weaknesses feedback, and goal-setting support. The paper also reports on the underlying transformer-based classifiers used to power the system.

The study involved 18 high school English Language Arts teachers from 4 schools in the United States. Teachers used DT after discussing literary texts in their classrooms; researchers collected audio-recorded discussions, had annotators hand-code transcripts, and then conducted a cognitive interview and survey-based usability evaluation with teachers. The study found that teachers perceived DT as helpful and easy to use, and that the automated classifiers achieved moderate to substantial agreement with human annotations, though performance was weaker for some collaboration labels.

Overall, the paper concludes that discussion analytics based on NLP can support teacher learning about student collaborative argumentation, but also notes the need for better classification performance, automated transcription/segmentation, and continued interface improvement before a fully automated end-to-end system is ready.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/usability field deployment with teacher surveys and cognitive interviews, plus separate classifier validation. It is peer-reviewed but not an experimental impact study on student outcomes, so credibility for causal claims is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports strong positive teacher perceptions and moderate-to-substantial classifier agreement, but no measured student learning gains or workload reduction effect sizes. Impact is promising but currently unclear for general K-12 settings.

interventions.use_case: classroom discussion analytics for teachers using NLP to classify student collaborative argumentation moves, specificity, and collaboration in high school discussions
teacher-facing learning analytics dashboard for coded discussion transcripts, collaboration maps, strengths/weaknesses, and goal-setting around student talk

finding.finding_summary: Teachers reported that Discussion Tracker was helpful for learning about and reflecting on student collaborative argumentation after a 15-minute demo and classroom use. On the post-use survey (n=18 teachers), the system’s analytics, annotated transcripts, and goal-setting features were rated favorably, with overall helpfulness at M=4.72/5 and the annotated transcript at M=4.89/5.
finding.measure: Teacher usability/helpfulness Likert survey after using the dashboard

finding.finding_summary: The system was explicitly designed to support teacher learning about students’ collaborative argumentation, a durable skill involving collaboration, questioning, and building on ideas. Teachers reported that DT helped them recognize student strengths and weaknesses in discussion and gave them more insight into student learning than they usually get from recalling the discussion.
finding.measure: Teacher survey ratings and cognitive interview reflections on understanding collaborative argumentation
